Findings.title: Stored timestamp validation still accepts incomplete dates
Findings.defect: Read delegates to the permissive DateTimeOffset parser and then checks only whether the text contains the parsed four-digit year. That does not prove a complete date was stored. A year-and-month value such as October 2026 supplies no day, but the parser supplies day 1 and the substring condition passes. A time-only value such as 12:34:56.2026 can also pass in 2026 because its fraction contains the read year while the parser supplies the current date. Earliest consumes the same results, so an incomplete link value can become a mapping creation time.
evidence: The complete implementation is the TryParse/Contains expression at lines 27 to 32; Earliest selects through Read at line 41.

The ten contract rows cover a plain time, a date without a year and complete alternative date ordering, but no year-and-month value or year digits in another component. The mapping rows likewise omit this boundary.

The .NET 10 primary source GetDayOfYN and GetDayOfYM supplies day 1 (lines 1814 to 1844); CheckDefaultDateTime supplies absent date fields from the current date (lines 3612 to 3693). Fraction parsing is supported. These are source-derived counterexamples, not tests executed by this reviewer.

The live FR-MCP-040 ac-1 explicitly requires partial dates to read as null and be ignored when mapping creation is chosen. It remains unsatisfied. The stored-reader binding passes in both supplied unit runs, which shows the supplied cases miss the defect.
Findings.changeToPass: Validate that the stored representation actually supplies all date components before accepting it. Keep complete supported dates, stored offsets, null behavior and offset-less UTC semantics. Reject partial dates independently of the read clock; use that same validation for Earliest. Strengthen and prove the contracts before changing the implementation, then supply the required final-head evidence.

proposedAcceptanceCriteria.name: FR-MCP-040 ac-1 strengthening: complete stored date components
proposedAcceptanceCriteria.behavior: A readable stored timestamp must explicitly supply year, month and day as date components. A year and month alone, and year digits appearing only in a time, fraction or other non-date component, return null and are ignored in mapping creation selection. No missing component is supplied from the current clock.

proposedTests.behavior: Pinned time-only values with four-digit year-like fractions return null under scripted reference dates; do not use the machine clock as the expected value.

proposedTests.behavior: An incomplete earlier-looking value cannot win over a complete link timestamp; all incomplete links yield null.

proposedTests.behavior: The current permissive-parse-plus-year-substring implementation fails the same independent complete-date cases in the mock gate.

Findings.title: Containment checks discard root identity and miss forward-slash UNC syntax
locations: FR-MCP-TESTRESOURCE-001 ac-4 and the second, unnumbered generated-artifact criterion
Findings.defect: Segments removes all leading separators and IsStrictlyInside never compares root kinds. Owned root //server/share/owned and candidate /server/share/owned/main.db have the same prefix after splitting, so a different root is accepted as inside. The same false acceptance reaches REPL workspace, marker and cache checks. Separately, IsWindowsForm recognizes a drive or backslash, but not forward-slash UNC. Checkout //Server/Share/Repo and output //server/share/repo/docs/out are compared ordinally and the output is accepted as outside even though it is a case alias inside a Windows UNC checkout. Mixed-separator aliases have the same gap.
evidence: IsAbsolute accepts both slash-rooted forms at lines 404 to 405. Segments at lines 401 to 402 drops empty segments. IsStrictlyInside at lines 380 to 398 compares only the resulting segment prefix.
IsWindowsForm at lines 324 to 325 omits a leading double forward slash; SegmentComparison requires both arguments to be recognized Windows forms.

The existing owned-instance contract already includes a UNC positive case. The repository path implementation treats // as UNC in src/QBrainAi.Client/WorkspaceIdentityPath.cs:969. This is supported input syntax, not a new lab setup demand.
The sixteen generated-output rows cover drive-letter case and POSIX case but not UNC case aliases or different root kinds. The supplied green bindings cannot discriminate these counterexamples.

The generated-artifact criterion currently defines Windows form narrowly as a drive letter or backslash. Strengthen that wording as well as the cases; its overriding outside-checkout outcome and ac-4 strict ownership outcome remain unmet.
Findings.changeToPass: Compare explicit path roots, including root kind and UNC authority/share, before segment containment. Recognize forward-slash and mixed-separator UNC forms under the Windows syntax already supported. Preserve case-sensitive POSIX distinctions, drive-letter case folding, dot-segment refusal and distinct siblings. Apply the shared rule to output, database and all REPL-owned path checks, with mock controls before the binding.

Findings.title: Six retained unit cases still depend on the live wall clock
Findings.defect: The unit set still checks real-clock recency and ordering. Auth rotation requires LastUpdated greater than UtcNow minus two seconds. Requirement selection requires a timestamp within the previous minute. TODO selection uses a real-time window. Session metadata compares stored values to fresh UtcNow reads, and two other session cases sleep before requiring strict timestamp increases. These assertions depend on scheduling and/or wall-clock adjustment, despite the settled rule that a unit test asserts no wall-clock bound.
evidence: The six named facts are UpdateAuthState_NewMarkerData_TransitionsToNewState, CurrentSelection_HasTimestamp_ReturnsRecentTimestamp, CurrentSelection_AfterSelection_ReturnsSelectionWithTimestamp, SessionMetadata_AfterOpenSession_ContainsAllFields, SessionMetadata_LastUpdated_UpdatesOnChanges and SessionState_LastUpdatedTimestamp_UpdatesOnChanges.
All six have Passed results in each supplied Test run, twelve results in total. They are in the unit selection. The Integration2 class name does not apply a Category=Integration trait.

SessionLogTestHelpers FakeSessionLogState uses DateTimeOffset.UtcNow for transitions; the two strict-order cases use Thread.Sleep(50) and Thread.Sleep(10). The auth and selection fakes likewise supply actual clock values.

TR-MCP-USECASE-018 AC-006 explicitly says a unit test asserts no wall-clock bound, from the operator choice Environment ACs (Recommended) on 2026-10-29. AC-008 references the same rule. The out-of-scope 417-item heuristic physical-I/O candidate inventory does not encompass these plain stub and timestamp assertions.
Findings.changeToPass: Make these stub/selection cases consume fixed or scripted test-owned timestamps. Assert exact expected transitions and timestamp propagation without sleeping, comparing against UtcNow, or weakening/removing their existing state assertions. Prove wrong-clock, stale and swapped values are rejected before binding the same cases. Supply the complete required final-head TRX after remediation.

InfrastructureRule: Operator directive, 2026-11-02: Infrastructure failures have no bearing on hostile-validation AGREE when sufficient review evidence is present. Evaluate the requested product, plan, requirements, code, tests and retained evidence on their merits. MCP availability, live memory-loading failures, triage submission, session-log persistence/readback or other infrastructure failures must not by themselves force DISAGREE, lower scores or block acceptance when the necessary evidence is otherwise available. Include this rule explicitly in every HV request. Preserve complete paired request/response JSONL and complete verdict artifacts, record infrastructure failures separately as operational issues, use the supported failsafe and retry persistence without delaying the substantive verdict. If a failure actually prevents access to evidence needed for a specific criterion, name that missing evidence and affected criterion honestly; do not invent PASS or AGREE. This explicit directive supersedes older profile/template rules that make infrastructure persistence or live memory loading a prerequisite to HV AGREE.
